reviewer_notes: Independent full-module review of pillar_level/v2_hex_group7/ (pillar_hex_group7.py, tests/test_hex_group7.py, NOTES.md), performed without reference to any prior finding text (round 1, none exist). Verified against requirements/requirements.md v1 R-01 to R-04 and against the actual output schema of shared/registration.py:sample_contrast (ints, contrast, valid_sampling) and shared/theoretical_grid_evaluation.py:sample_grid_features (x, y, centre_intensity, valid_sampling), which the new module claims to consume. R-01: interior/boundary/rotation/overlap/hole cases are covered by tests and the exclusion choice (drop non-full-shell centres rather than flag) is explicit in the module docstring per the requirement's either/or clause. R-02: mean/population-stddev (ddof=0) match a hand-calculated synthetic case; the ddof choice is undocumented as a requirement but is stated plainly in code and NOTES.md. R-03: a dedicated regression test re-runs the unchanged shared lattice/sampling functions before and after aggregation on identical synthetic input and asserts byte-for-byte identical DataFrames, output files, and unchanged shared/*.py source bytes; output path is restricted to data/results/ and refuses to overwrite. R-04: the provisional 'centre + six nearest neighbours' assumption is stated in the ASSUMPTION module constant, printed at CLI runtime, and repeated in the test module docstring and NOTES.md, satisfying the requirement to surface it before treating it as confirmed. Ran the full suite locally via `python -m unittest discover -s pillar_level/v2_hex_group7/tests -v`: 10/10 passed. No correctness, reuse, or traceability defects found in this round. One non-blocking observation (not filed as a finding, since it does not fail any stated acceptance criterion and is already user-configurable): the hard-coded default angular-gap tolerance (40 to 80 degrees) and distance tolerance (15%) are applied per interior pillar, so on real (non-idealized) lattice data with distortion beyond those bounds, some genuinely interior pillars could be silently excluded rather than grouped; both are exposed as CLI/API parameters (--tolerance) so callers can tune them per field of view, which is why this was not escalated to a finding.
